Chapter 7: Building a Mission — Finding Purpose Through Small Bets.
So, you’ve built up your skills and found your groove with a bit of autonomy. What comes next? It’s time to think about your mission — that bigger “why” behind the work you do. Now, I know, “mission” can sound kind of overwhelming, right? But here’s the thing: it doesn’t have to feel so intimidating. Most of the time, purpose isn’t about one huge lightbulb moment. Instead, it grows out of a bunch of small, thoughtful experiments.
Imagine you’re navigating a river. You’re not just jumping in and hoping for the best — you’re making a series of small, careful moves, testing the water in different directions. Each of these “small bets” is really just a low-risk experiment — a way to see what feels right before you commit to anything big.
Let’s take a teacher as an example. Maybe they’re already awesome in the classroom. But now, they start dabbling in curriculum design, or maybe they get involved in community outreach, or even play around with educational technology. Little by little, by trying these different things, they start to figure out what really excites them — what feels both meaningful and impactful. And before long, a mission starts to take shape. Maybe it’s advocating for equal access to education, or creating new tools to make learning more fun and effective.
So, how do you actually build your mission through these small bets? Here’s a simple approach:
First, look for those sweet spots — places where your skills match up with new opportunities or real needs around you.
Then, launch a few small projects or team up with others to try out new ideas. Don’t think of it as a big commitment — just a chance to experiment.
After each one, take a step back and ask yourself, “Which activities felt most energizing? Where did I make the biggest difference?”
Use that feedback — and the real results you see — to gently adjust your path. Over time, this process helps you shape a mission that actually fits your strengths and what you care about.
The beauty of this way of working is that it takes the pressure off. You don’t have to “find your purpose” overnight. Instead, you get to be curious, stay flexible, and learn as you go. And as your mission gets clearer, you’ll notice your efforts start to line up with what matters most to you — making a bigger impact, and finding a deeper sense of fulfillment along the way.
